guide.title: Field Diagnostic Guide
guide.subtitle: How to use DRISHYA correctly in the field.
guide.using_step1_desc: Select Turmeric or Citrus from the home screen. DRISHYA uses separate models trained specifically for each crop.
guide.using_step2_desc: Frame a single, clearly visible leaf in natural daylight. Capture the affected area as clearly as possible.
guide.using_step3_desc: Tap "Check a Leaf" and upload or capture your photograph. DRISHYA will examine the image.
guide.using_step4_desc: Review the diagnosis headline, any visual attention mapping if available, and the notes below. If the result says Unclear, retake your photo.
guide.using_step5_desc: Each completed check is saved to your personal My Leaf Journal for future reference.
guide.photo_tips_subtitle: Good photographs lead to better results.
guide.tip_one_leaf_desc: Frame a single leaf so that the affected area is fully visible in the shot.
guide.tip_light_desc: Photograph in open daylight. Avoid harsh shadows, flashlight glare, or photographing in dim indoor conditions.
guide.tip_focus_desc: Ensure leaf veins and surface textures are crisp and in focus before capturing.
guide.tip_glare_desc: Strong reflections can obscure leaf surface details. Slight shade without blocking light works well.
guide.tip_center_desc: Position the leaf so that the main affected region is near the center of the frame.
guide.understanding_condition_desc: DRISHYA identifies the most likely condition from the supported class list for that crop. For Turmeric: Healthy, Leaf Blotch, Leaf Spot, or Dry Leaf. For Citrus: one of 18 possible findings including diseases, pests, mites, and deficiency-related conditions.
guide.understanding_unclear_desc: If the model's raw softmax probability falls below the safety rejection threshold (0.65), DRISHYA marks the result as Unclear rather than guessing. This is a safety feature. Retake your photo in better conditions or consult a local expert.
guide.understanding_attention_desc: When visual attention mapping is available, DRISHYA shows the areas of the leaf that received greater model attention during prediction. This is generated using Grad-CAM, a gradient-based visualization technique.
guide.understanding_attention_caveat: Important: This highlights model attention during prediction, not a proven cause of the condition. It is a research aid, not a diagnostic proof.
guide.expert_help_intro: DRISHYA is a research prototype, not a certified agricultural diagnostic service. Always consult an agricultural expert before making treatment decisions.
guide.expert_help_unclear: If the result is Unclear — retake your photo first, then consult a local expert if the result remains inconclusive.
guide.expert_help_mismatch: If symptoms in the field do not match the result — trust your direct field observation and consult a Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) officer.
guide.expert_help_serious: For serious or widespread crop issues — seek professional field assessment immediately.
guide.expert_help_treatment: Before any treatment decision — always consult a qualified agronomist or extension officer. DRISHYA does not provide treatment prescriptions.
guide.expert_help_kvk: Your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) provides free expert field advisory services for farmers.
guide.can_do_1: Analyze supported Turmeric and Citrus leaf photographs.
guide.can_do_2: Provide a model-based classification result from the supported condition list.
guide.can_do_3: Show visual attention mapping when explanation data is available.
guide.can_do_4: Maintain your personal authenticated diagnosis history in My Leaf Journal.
guide.can_do_5: Flag uncertain predictions rather than providing a low-confidence guess.
guide.cannot_do_1: Cannot guarantee a correct field diagnosis.
guide.cannot_do_2: Cannot replace the judgment of a qualified agricultural expert.
guide.cannot_do_3: Cannot provide treatment prescriptions, pesticide recommendations, or dosage guidance.
guide.cannot_do_5: Cannot establish causation from visual attention maps.
guide.cannot_do_6: Cannot diagnose conditions outside its supported class list.
guide.kvk_info: For persistent symptoms, consult your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK).

about.title: About DRISHYA
about.subtitle: A research prototype for explainable crop condition detection.
about.why_desc: Turmeric and Citrus are high-value crops critical to rural livelihoods in India. Leaf disease identification traditionally relies on visual inspection or occasional expert visits — leaving farmers without timely diagnosis support. DRISHYA is a research system that combines deep learning inference, uncertainty rejection gating, visual attention mapping, and multilingual output to support — not replace — field judgement.
about.how_works_1: You photograph a leaf in the field.
about.how_works_2: The image is validated and prepared (resized to model input resolution, normalized using standard ImageNet statistics).
about.how_works_3: A PyTorch inference session runs the appropriate crop-specific model on CPU.
about.how_works_4: Softmax probabilities are evaluated across candidate classes (temperature scaling calibration is currently inactive).
about.how_works_5: A safety gate checks model probability against the 0.65 threshold. If probability is below the threshold, the result is marked as Unclear.
about.how_works_6: When available, Grad-CAM generates a visual attention map highlighting areas of greater model attention.
about.how_works_7: The result is returned and saved to your personal Leaf Journal.
about.crops_turmeric_classes: 4 conditions: Healthy, Leaf Blotch, Leaf Spot, Dry Leaf
about.crops_citrus_classes: 18 findings: including diseases, insect pests, mites, and deficiency-related conditions
about.models_note: DRISHYA uses one dedicated model per supported crop. Only one model per crop is active for inference at a time.
about.models_pretrained_note: Both models use ImageNet-pretrained weights (IMAGENET1K_V1) as the starting point, fine-tuned on the respective crop datasets.
about.explainability_desc: When visual attention mapping is available, DRISHYA shows areas of the leaf image that received greater model attention during prediction. This is generated using Grad-CAM (Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping).
about.explainability_caveat: This highlights model attention, not a proven cause of the condition. It is a research visualization aid, not diagnostic proof or confirmation of causation.
about.responsible_1: DRISHYA is a research prototype. It is not a certified agricultural diagnostic service.
about.responsible_2: All predictions are subject to model uncertainty. Low-confidence results are explicitly flagged as Unclear.
about.responsible_3: DRISHYA does not make autonomous treatment decisions. Human expert oversight is essential.
about.responsible_4: Model performance on real-world field images may differ from research dataset evaluation.
about.responsible_5: DRISHYA should be used as a supplementary reference tool, not as a standalone diagnostic authority.
about.privacy_1: DRISHYA requires authentication. Your diagnosis history is strictly scoped to your own account.
about.privacy_2: Prediction metadata (crop, result, confidence, model used, date) is stored in your personal history.
about.privacy_3: A SHA-256 fingerprint of your uploaded image is recorded for provenance, but the original image bytes are not permanently stored by the history system.
about.privacy_4: DRISHYA does not share your diagnosis history with other users.
about.prototype_desc: DRISHYA is a research and development prototype. It has not been certified, validated, or endorsed by ICAR, any KVK, or any governmental agricultural authority as a field-certified diagnostic service. Evaluation results reported during research are dataset-specific and do not constitute a guarantee of real-world field performance.
about.prototype_disclaimer: Always consult a qualified agricultural expert before making crop management or treatment decisions.
about.description: DRISHYA (Deep Robust Intelligence for Sustainable Harvest & Yield Assessment) provides explainable crop pathology intelligence for farmers and researchers.
about.mission: Bridging deep learning research and practical field agriculture with transparency and safety.
